title: What 30 Years With Warren Buffett Taught Me - Gisela Baur
description:
📗 FREE GUIDE: 15 lessons from 30 years with Warren Buffett
https://go.good-investing.net/gisela-buffett?utm_source=youtube&utm_medium=description&utm_campaign=lm-gisela-buffett

In the 1990s, German financial journalist Gisela Baur sent Warren Buffett a 10-page letter full of numbers. Two weeks later, a fax arrived: "Why don't you come over to the meeting?" She has been going to Omaha ever since and was one of the first non-American journalists to interview him.

In this talk from the first Good Investing Night in Munich, Gisela shares what 30 years of contact with Buffett taught her:

- Buffett's photographic memory: he knew every number in her letter
- How he decides within seconds who he lets into his circle, and then holds on
- A simple view of business: "A company is an organization which wants to employ capital to make gains."
- Charlie Munger's one-word answer to how Berkshire runs with so few people: trust. Judge first, then trust.
- Why Buffett stays happy: a simple base in Omaha, and the courage to give things up when they are over

The talk ends with a short Q&A on why she never bought Berkshire shares as a journalist.
